headline: Full Chuba Drops 157 on mikelanta, Burrow's 36.88 Tops the League as Brent Looking 4 His Keys Wins by 0.66
meme_brief: Two teams decide a game by less than a point while across town mikelanta gets buried by 61, and everybody's bench somehow outscored their starters this week.
recap:
The headline result of Week 7 is also the closest: Brent Looking 4 His Keys edged Ja'Marr Ja'Merrier 124.3 to 123.64, a margin of 0.66 points. Malik Willis went off for 30.02 points as the top scorer on the winning roster, while Ja'Marr Ja'Merrier got 27.1 from Trey McBride and 26.42 from Michael Penix Jr. and still came up just short. There was no bench-decision villain on the losing side — their lineup choices were clean — but the winners can't say the same (more on that below).

The other end of the spectrum belonged to Full Chuba, who put up 157.88 and buried mikelanta by 61.14, the week's largest margin. Joe Burrow's 36.88 points led not just Full Chuba but the entire league, with Tony Pollard chipping in 35.0 on the same roster. mikelanta got 26.12 from Caleb Williams and still never had a chance. Silverbacks (100 vs 1) also put together a big one, dropping 147.04 on Playing for 2027 in a 40.54-point win, with Jaxon Smith-Njigba's 26.8 pacing that roster.

Bench management was rough across the board. The most expensive mistake belonged to Brent Looking 4 His Keys, who sat Tre Tucker and his 18.8 points in favor of Aaron Jones Sr., who managed only 3.1 — a 15.7-point gap in a game their team won by less than one point anyway, so it cost them nothing but dignity. The Josh Allens left 18.4 points on the bench by starting Nico Collins (1.6) over Omar Cooper Jr. (20.0) in a loss to NateDawg726, and Silverbacks (100 vs 1) benched Quinshon Judkins (22.9) in favor of J.K. Dobbins (8.3), a 14.6-point gift that didn't end up mattering in a blowout win.

Elsewhere, demon44 fell to LaHorrible by 9.9 points despite Drake Maye's 32.44, and Theme From The Bottom were run over by Kirkumcised Penix, 102.28 to 62.44, with Deshaun Watson quietly outscoring every starter on that roster from the bench with 19.22 points nobody used.
transaction_desk:
Most of the week's activity cost nothing, and it showed. Every free-agent move logged this week went through uncontested, meaning no team actually burned real waiver priority chasing a difference-maker — the only exception was demon44's claim on Greg Dulcich at tight end, though the data doesn't show what priority position that cost them. He scored zero points in his first week on the roster, so there's nothing to grade yet either way.

mikelanta was the week's most active shop, cycling through three moves at the same position — dropping Kayshon Boutte for Jordan Whittington, then flipping Whittington for Tutu Atwell within the same week, before adding Sean Tucker as a separate move. None of it cost anything in priority, and the one player who actually played, Sean Tucker, produced 11.2 points that could have started over Jalen Coker's 1.4 — a decision mikelanta is already on record making incorrectly this week.

Playing for 2027's double move drew the week's only flagged pattern: dropping Austin Ekeler to add Andrew Armstrong, who shares a backfield with Rashee Rice's teammate in Kansas City — a depth stash that fits a known pattern for that team. It produced 0.8 points in its debut week, which is about what a speculative add at no cost should be expected to do. Ja'Marr Ja'Merrier's free pickup of Tyler Huntley quietly paid off immediately, with 18.12 points as a free, zero-cost add — the best value of the week by a wide margin given it cost nothing at all.

standings_narrative:
Five seeds are locked in by record right now: Ja'Marr Ja'Merrier at 6-1 holds the top spot, followed by Silverbacks (100 vs 1) and NateDawg726 at 5-2, then The Josh Allens and LaHorrible both at 4-3. The sixth and final playoff seed currently belongs to Full Chuba, who sit at 3-4 but lead all remaining teams in total points for the season, giving them the points-based tiebreaker over everyone else outside the top five records. That cushion is real but not huge — Full Chuba's scoring lead over the next team in that group is 62.78 points.

Right behind them, demon44 sits as the closest threat to that sixth seed on points, two games back of the fifth seed in the standings but within range if Full Chuba cools off. Brent Looking 4 His Keys sits at 4-3 as well but currently outside the picture entirely since the playoff math runs on record first for the top five — their point total isn't enough to leapfrog Full Chuba for the points seed. Mikelanta, Kirkumcised Penix, Playing for 2027, and Theme From The Bottom round out the group on the outside looking in, with Theme From The Bottom at 1-6 facing the longest odds of the bunch.
look_ahead:
Week 8 features a rematch angle worth watching: Ja'Marr Ja'Merrier, fresh off their heartbreak loss, draws mikelanta, who just got buried by 61 points last week. Full Chuba and NateDawg726 face off in what should be one of the week's higher-scoring games given both offenses showed out this past week. Brent Looking 4 His Keys, winners by less than a point, now face LaHorrible, while The Josh Allens get a shot at Silverbacks (100 vs 1) after their own bench-management stumble.

Kirkumcised Penix and Playing for 2027 meet after very different weeks — a blowout win for one side and a blowout loss for the other. Theme From The Bottom look for their second win against demon44, and both teams enter with plenty to prove after rough showings.
